=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): opposite (clearly visible as paired leaves attached at the same node along the stem)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): distal (leaves are spaced along the stem with distinct internodes, rather than being bunched together)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3.	Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade without subdivisions)
    4.	Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5.	Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6.	Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7.	Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (the leaf edges appear smooth and continuous without teeth)
    8.	Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (the leaves are broadly oval-shaped with the widest point near the middle)
    9.	Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (the tip of the leaf tapers to a distinct point)
    10.	Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (the base of the leaf narrows down to the petiole, appearing somewhat wedge-shaped)
    11.	Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a central midrib is visible with secondary veins branching off it)
    12.	Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): clearly visible and well-spaced (the secondary veins form an open network extending towards the margin)
    13.	Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (the leaf surface reflects light, indicating a glossy texture)
    14.	Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs or fuzz on the leaf surface)
    15.	Petiole length (short / long): short (the stalks attaching the leaves to the stem are relatively short compared to the leaf blade)
    16.	Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (the petioles appear cylindrical and round in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17.	Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (the stems appear thin, green, and flexible, lacking the thickness of woody tissue)
    18.	Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (the stems appear smooth without visible hairs)
    19.	Stem color: green (the stems are a vibrant green color)
    20.	Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (the stems appear uniform without ridges or lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21.	Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are visible at the leaf bases)
    22.	Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no exudate is visible)
    23.	Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint-like structure is visible at the leaf base)
    24.	Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils are visible)
F. Notes: Several leaves display distinct yellowish, winding lines (mining damage) and some leaf margins show irregular missing sections.
